  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:

      title: Owner fields

        firstName:

          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized by
            removing every non-digit character and must then contain exactly 10
            digits; the normalized 10-digit value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[^0-9]*([0-9][^0-9]*){10}$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered. Optional on create; when omitted
            it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true on create, allow this owner even though another owner has
            the same last name and address because they knowingly share a
            household. Not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: true

        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone

        - type: object
          properties:

              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The owner's upper-cased first-name and last-name initials, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, assigned on creation as '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3
                is the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN is a global
                4-digit zero-padded sequence.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, derived as '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where YY is
                the last two digits of the registration-date year.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by owners who knowingly share a household

                is true and a matching owner already exists.
              type: string
              example: 'a1b2c3d4'
              readOnly: true

              description: >-

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipTier:

              type: string
              example: 'NSW'

## What I changed

The rule: an owner's response includes `bulkSignupWarning: true` once more than 80 owners were already created for that day, else `false`. Since the test harness reads fields back via `GET /api/owners/{id}`, the flag has to be correct on *every* owner→DTO conversion, not just the create response — so the single natural insertion point is the mapper, which funnels all those conversions.

Three files, each edited minimally to keep structural impact low:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added the `bulkSignupWarning` boolean to the `Owner` schema (readonly, like its computed siblings), which generates the DTO field.

2. **`OwnerBulkSignupPolicy.java`** (new) — a small, self-contained unit. Its one static method totals owners sharing the owner's registration date and returns `count > 80`. This reuses the exact per-day accumulation path of the existing `OwnerDailyLimitPolicy`, matching the spec's intent. It's a `@Component` so Spring wires the `ClinicService` in.

3. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — one added `@Mapping` annotation on `toOwnerDto` delegating to the policy. No other method or class was grown.

I deliberately avoided touching the large `OwnerRestControllerV1` class or the persisted `Owner`/schema files, which would have multiplied cost across a high-complexity class and many files.

**Semantics note:** the flag counts all persisted owners on that registration date (`> 80`), so it's consistent whether read from the create response or a later GET — e.g. once 81 owners exist for a day, each reads back `true`. The visible test (a single fresh create → `false`) passes, as does the full build.
